recommendation: Keep this no-change audit as-is. Future work should address only specific later Device, DeviceDefinition, or UDI trackers; FHIR-13965 itself does not identify a remaining current-spec source defect.
issue_request: FHIR-13965 was a Published, Persuasive STU3 Device issue asking how complex, dynamically configurable devices with multiple subsystem UDIs should be represented. The final resolution said the concern was already handled because Device and DeviceDefinition UDI data were 0..*, with the broader Device/DeviceComponent merge providing the component modeling path.
initial_application: No local source-history commit explicitly mentions FHIR-13965. Jira recorded an October 2018 comment that the issue was already applied. The application appears to have been through the broader 2018 Device rework: DeviceDefinition was added, Device was changed, DeviceComponent was removed from active build listings, and Device narrative was updated to model components as Device resources linked by Device.parent.
additional_context: Device and DeviceDefinition are active OO-owned resources in source/fhir.ini, while DeviceComponent is commented out/dropped. Current Device source allows Device.udiCarrier 0..*, says a physical unit can consist of modules represented by multiple Device resources bound through parent, and defines Device.parent for module hierarchies. Current DeviceDefinition source allows multiple udiDeviceIdentifier entries and multiple packaging UDI identifiers. Device narrative and DeviceDefinition narrative describe whole-device/component hierarchies for complex point-of-care devices. Related FHIR-15812 and FHIR-16960 audit commits are already present on the combined branch and support the same conclusion.
reconciliation: Published empty audit commit 6691c151bbc45c730ab1923c0e4aa970ad2b8e56 with no source changes because the current source already satisfies FHIR-13965.
